newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Arrest sought for aides to S.Korea president's son.
newsitem.headline: Arrest sought for aides to S.Korea president's son.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Wednesday sought arrest warrants for close associates of President Kim Young-sam's son, state radio said.

The prosecutors filed a request with a Seoul criminal court for warrants to arrest two business friends of Kim Hyun-chul on bribery charges, it said. The prosecutors have been trying to build a case against the younger Kim.

The radio said Kim Hi-chan and Park Tae-joong were charged with accepting bribes from other businessmen in return for promises they would ask the president's second son to help them obtain government licences for broadcasting projects.
Prosecutors were not immediately available for comment on the report but they said earlier they would seek to arrest the two associates.
Prosecutors have said Park has denied accusations by opposition politicians that he acted as a bagman for bribes from various companies on behalf of Kim Hyun-chul.
Prosecutor-general Kim Ki-soo said on Tuesday the prosecution planned to summon Kim Hyun-chul by next week for questioning over allegations of irregularities.
